definition: In statistics, multivariate adaptive regression splines (MARS) is a form of regression analysis introduced by Jerome H.
details: Friedman in 1991. It is a non-parametric regression technique and can be seen as an extension of linear models that automatically models nonlinearities and interactions between variables. The term "MARS" is trademarked and licensed to Salford Systems. In order to avoid trademark infringements, many open-source implementations of MARS are called "Earth".

explainer.lead: Multivariate adaptive regression splines (MARS) is a non-parametric regression technique introduced by Jerome H. Friedman in 1991 that automatically models nonlinearities and interactions between variables. It matters as an extension of linear models that captures nonlinear structure without hand-specifying it.

tiers.eli5: It fits a curve through data by joining straight pieces at chosen breakpoints, automatically deciding where to bend instead of forcing one straight line.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it when linear models underfit due to nonlinearity or interaction effects. A pitfall is naming and licensing: the term "MARS" is trademarked and licensed to Salford Systems, so many open-source implementations are called "Earth".
tiers.paperLevel: MARS is a form of non-parametric regression that extends linear models by automatically modelling nonlinearities and interactions between variables. Being non-parametric, it does not assume a fixed functional form for the relationship.

explainer.example: A regression on several input variables where MARS automatically introduces bends and interaction terms rather than assuming a single linear fit.
